items.headline: China's anthropomorphic-AI rules force Doubao and Qwen to switch off user-created agents
items.diff_narrative: This is a wholly new storyline with no antecedent yesterday, which was dominated by an inference-throughput release and three funding/M&A items. It pivots the day's lead from capability and capital to regulation: ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen both notified users over the July 3-6 weekend that user-created agent features will go dark ahead of China's Interim Measures on AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services (effective July 15), with Qwen disabling humanlike and user-created agents July 10 and Doubao giving users until October 15 to export data. The structural hook, that persistent identity and long-horizon memory are now a regulated surface being resolved by withdrawal rather than redesign, has no counterpart in the prior day's coverage.

items.headline: ICML 2026 opens in Seoul with a record submission pile and agent safety at the center
items.diff_narrative: New today and directly tied to a calendar shift: yesterday's events roundup treated the July 6 window as Geneva AI Week, whereas today ICML 2026 in Seoul becomes its own lead item as it actually opens July 6 at COEX. The reporting goes beyond a listing to a substantive angle absent yesterday, a record 23,918 submissions with 6,352 accepted, agentic-safety research as the field's center of gravity, and watermark-based reviewer policing that flagged 398 reviewers and triggered 497 desk rejections.

items.headline: Etched steps out of stealth with an $800M war chest and a transformer-only inference ASIC
items.diff_narrative: A net-new company entering the same non-NVIDIA inference-silicon thread the prior day tracked through Tenstorrent and Stathera, but as a fresh stealth-exit event rather than a continuation. Where yesterday's silicon items were an M&A denial (Jim Keller ruling out a Qualcomm buyout of Tenstorrent) and an early-stage $55M MEMS-timing raise sampling in 2028, Etched's disclosure is a shipping-adjacent working chip on TSMC N4P, $800M raised, a $5B valuation, and more than $1B in contracts signed before first shipment. The coincidental $800M figure is shared with yesterday's Together AI round but is otherwise unrelated. The through-line the day advances is that inference-specialized ASICs now attract billion-dollar order books pre-shipment.

items.headline: AI events to plan around now
items.diff_narrative: The only genuine carryover from yesterday, and it has rotated at the front while the back half holds steady. The near-term anchor swaps from Geneva AI Week (July 6-10, now dropped as it is underway) to ICML in Seoul (July 6-11) as the immediate research item; the July 8 AI Tinkerers San Francisco meetup with Attio persists unchanged as the local pick. The standing tracks, Hot Chips (Aug 23-25), AI Infra Summit (Sept 15-17), the early-August security block (AI Risk Summit, Black Hat, DEF CON AI Village), Ai4 (Aug 4-6), GitHub Universe, and AWS re:Invent, are the same slate carried forward, and today additionally names the ACM AI Leadership Summit and OWASP Global AppSec USA in the same list.
